findings: design/design.md:1 and design/contract.json:3 identify the checked-in Design as R-0002, while design/contract.json:203-207 retains the prior team and candidate fingerprints. The active requirement is R-0001 and expressly rejects former Design authority at specs/spec.md:33,83,86, so the existing privacy assertions cannot establish current collection, flow, retention, deletion, default, or ownership decisions.

design/design.md:23-27 and design/contract.json:145-157 make telemetry, agent-activity, and Retro evidence durable across cleanup, but the only privacy treatment is the prose risk mitigation at design/contract.json:186. It does not define a field-level private-versus-portable allowlist, forbidden-field rejection, pseudonym linkability boundary, retention duration and trigger, deletion propagation to downstream copies, cleanup receipt, or accountable privacy decision owner. That leaves no failing-capable proof that exports exclude secrets, full prompts/transcripts, predecessor private runtime, and copied authentication authority as required by specs/spec.md:37,85,106.
decisions: Regenerate the privacy design under the active R-0001 candidate. Inventory each collected field and data flow across private run state, dashboards, telemetry, agent activity, diagnostics, Retro, and release artifacts; record purpose, necessity, access boundary, privacy-protective default, applicable opt-out or non-applicability rationale, retention owner, and downstream deletion behavior.

Define exact portable schemas as positive allowlists: emit provenance references and safe reason codes instead of copied prompts, transcripts, private runtime, credentials, authentication receipts, or free-form diagnostic payloads; reject forbidden fields before persistence/export and make pseudonymous identifiers unlinkable outside the bounded run purpose.

Bind FP-AC20 and J6 to current positive and severed selectors that inject representative secrets, prompts, private paths, identities, copied authority, and duplicate/replay events; prove minimized exports, single-counted usage, explicit unavailable values, idempotent retention/deletion through every downstream copy, preserved evidence on cleanup failure, and an attributable deletion/minimization receipt.
